name: Equinoid
body:
Equinoids are tall humanoids often likened to minotaurs but with heads like those of horses, donkeys, zebras, or similar equine animals.

Appearance

Equinoids are amazingly diverse in appearance. Most have heads that look like horses, zebras, or other Earthly equine creatures, the coloration blending seamlessly into human skin tones along their limbs and torsos, while manes of horsehair flow down their backs. However, their coloration can vary, as some rare specimens have been known to come in shades of lavender, or rainbow-striped patterns-perhaps due to the influence of arcane of fey bloodlines.

Equinoids have hooves instead of feet. They are always toned and athletic, and beautiful by both human and equine standards. They are usually quite proud, and take pains to maintain their clothing and armor to the finest standards.

Social

Equinoids are a rare species, and it is uncertain where they originated. Some believe they are indeed an offshoot of minotaurs, or a similarly cursed species, but the more commonly accepted theory is that some arcane experiment or fey bargain led to their evolution.

Equinoids form small communities, usually near or within larger settlements of other humanoids. They compulsively seek the respect of others; while they often squabble amongst each other, they usually present a united front when dealing with other humanoids.

Equinoids are often accused of seeking glory at the expense of accomplishing practical goals. Many choose a life in the public eye, becoming politicians, emissaries, prominent business leaders, or noteworthy explorers. Those who choose the life of a warrior often become daredevil adventurers, mercenaries, or gladiators.

Equinoids hate to be compared to centaurs, minotaurs, or common horses. They can tolerate most humanoids, but harbor a deep enmity against goblins.

Alignment and Religion

Equinoids value their independence above all, and hate to be told what to do. They lean toward Chaotic alignments, with no preference toward Good or Evil.

They have no particular religious traditions or tendencies. Each equinoid makes their own decisions in this matter-often starting with their parents’ faith and adding bits and pieces to it from the religions they see in the communities around them.

Names

Some typical equinoid names include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Aarod, 2 Argentina, 3 Blanco, 4 Breva, 5 Nelle, 6 Renegade, 7 Rojack, 8 Spirit, 9 Thunder, 10 Viento, 11 Whinnie, 12 Zed

Common Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are athletic and imposing, but headstrong. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Cha, -2 Wis [standard]. (0)
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Monstrous Humanoid. (3)
Speed Your base speed is 40 feet. (1)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Equinoid. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Elven, Giant, Gnoll, Goblin, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Traits
Bite You have strong jaws, allowing you to make a bite attack. This is a primary natural weapon that deals 1d4 damage. (2)
Darkvision You have darkvision 60 feet. (-)
Presence You gain a +2 species bonus to Diplomacy and Intimidate checks. (4)
Push/Pull You treat your Strength score as 4 points higher when calculating how much weight you can drag (usually 5 times your maximum load). Additionally, you receive a +2 species bonus when making Strength checks to break items, and to your CMB when attempting a bull rush or drag maneuver. Such maneuvers provoke attacks of opportunity as usual unless you have a feat or ability that prevents them from doing so. (2)
Total: 12 RP (advanced)
Alternate Traits
Jittery You lack the confidence of many of your kin, instead making sure to always be aware of any danger nearby. You gain Lightning Reflexes as a bonus feat and a +2 species bonus to all Perception checks. This trait replaces presence.
Hooves You can make a kick attack with one of your hooves. This is a secondary attack that deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage. You cannot use this ability if you’re wearing soft boots, but you can if you’re wearing horseshoes. This trait replaces bite.
Engineer While most equinoids are good at getting people to do what they want, you are skilled at making machines work for you. You gain a +2 bonus to Intelligence instead of Charisma, and a +2 species bonus to Disable Device and Knowledge (engineering) checks. This trait alters ability score modifiers and replaces presence.
Nimble While most equinoids are built for strength, you are built to be fast and agile. You gain a +2 bonus to Dexterity instead of Strength, a +2 species bonus to all Acrobatics checks, and Run as a bonus feat. This trait alters ability score modifiers and replaces presence.
Weapon Familiarity You are proficient with the gladius, glaive, halberd, and short sword. You treat the fauchard, shotel, and sica as martial weapons instead of exotic ones. This trait replaces push/pull.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1 to your total number of rage rounds per day.
Bard Add a +1/2 bonus on Diplomacy checks to gather information and a +1/2 bonus on Intimidate checks to demoralize.
Bloodrager Add +1 foot to your base speed. In combat, this benefit has an effect only after every five such increases in base speed. This bonus stacks with your fast movement class feature, and applies under the same conditions as that feature.
Cavalier Add +1/4 to your banner bonus.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or drag attempt.
Oracle Reduce the penalty for not being proficient for one weapon by 1. When the nonproficiency penalty for a weapon becomes 0 because of this ability, you are treated as having the appropriate Martial or Exotic Weapon Proficiency feat for that weapon.
Paladin Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using smite evil (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Acrobatics checks to jump and a +1/2 bonus on Intimidate checks to demoralize enemies.
Skald Add +1 to your total number of raging song rounds per day.
Sorcerer Select one bloodline power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that bloodline power.
Swashbuckler Increase the number of times per day you can use charmed life by +1/4.
Vigilante Gain +1/3 on all Acrobatics, Perception, and Stealth checks in areas of plains terrain.

Awesome Ancestries: Fantasy Animal Humanoids, Vol. 3 - Born to Be Wild. © 2025, Far Distant Future Publishing; Author: Bryan Mangum.
